title: Copy a folder with cp -r (fixes "cp: -r not specified; omitting directory")
summary: cp refuses to copy a folder unless you add -r (recursive), which tells it to copy the folder together with everything inside it. Add -r before the source and destination.

aliases.text: how to copy a folder in linux terminal

steps.explain: Check that the thing you want to copy is a folder. A d at the start of the line means it is a folder.

placeholders.name: SOURCE_DIR
placeholders.description: The folder you want to copy

steps.expect: A line starting with d, for example drwxr-xr-x ... photos

steps.explain: Copy the folder and everything inside it. -r (recursive) is the flag that lets cp copy a folder; without it cp stops with the error above. If DEST_DIR does not exist, it becomes the copy. If DEST_DIR already exists, the copy goes inside it.

placeholders.name: SOURCE_DIR
placeholders.description: The folder you want to copy

placeholders.name: DEST_DIR
placeholders.description: Name of the new copy, or of an existing folder to copy into

steps.expect: No message appears and the prompt comes back; the folder is copied.

alternatives.explain: Capital -R means the same as -r for cp: copy directories recursively.

placeholders.name: SOURCE_DIR
placeholders.description: The folder you want to copy

placeholders.name: DEST_DIR
placeholders.description: Name of the new copy, or of an existing folder to copy into

alternatives.expect: Same as the main command: the folder is copied with no message.

warnings: If DEST_DIR already contains files with the same names, cp -r overwrites them without asking.
